name: PixiTween Director S05a: deterministic review rules
description: Pure, offline review rules: an engine geometry model (layerBoxAt), text-box estimate, contrast maths, pixel samplers, rules R1-R5 with numeric evidence, computed and self-verified suggested fixes, and a six-case synthetic calibration set. No model calls, no browser. The contract entry point is runRules(comp, assets, opts) in server/review/rules.ts (decision D-10), a thin node-side wrapper over the isomorphic rules-core.ts. Leaves out frame capture, Spark visual review and the fix loop (prd-s05b-review-visual).

userStories.title: Pixel samplers (plate luminance, mask coverage)
userStories.description: As a rules author, I want sampled pixel statistics from stored assets so that contrast and occlusion use real pixels.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md section 5.3 (region mapping, 256 px downsample) and server/media/image.ts (imageSize).

Create server/review/pixels.ts exporting makeSharpPixelDeps(readAsset: (assetId: string) => Promise<Buffer>): Required<Pick<RuleDeps,'plateLuminance'|'maskCoverage'>>. Both decode the asset with sharp once per id (cache), downscale to at most 256 px on the long side, and take a region in NORMALISED 0..1 coordinates. plateLuminance returns the mean over the region of per-pixel LINEAR relative luminance (use a 256-entry linearisation table); maskCoverage returns the fraction of region pixels whose grey (or alpha when the PNG has alpha) is >= 128. A region that is empty after clamping to 0..1 throws RangeError('empty region').
Create server/review/pixels.test.ts that builds solid-colour and half-and-half PNGs with sharp (create) in memory; no fixture files are needed.
acceptanceCriteria: Solid grey 30, 120 and 230 PNGs give plateLuminance over {0,0,1,1} within 0.002 of 0.013, 0.1878 and 0.7913
A PNG whose left half is grey 30 and right half grey 230 gives a mean within 0.003 of 0.4022 over the full region and within 0.002 of 0.013 over {left:0,top:0,right:0.5,bottom:1}
A mask PNG with the left half 255 and the right half 0 gives maskCoverage 0.5 (within 0.01) over the full region, 1 over the left half and 0 over the right half
A region {left:0.4,top:0.4,right:0.4,bottom:0.9} rejects with RangeError; two calls with the same asset id call readAsset once

userStories.title: Rule R1: text over or behind the product
userStories.description: As a viewer, I want text that neither sits on the product nor is hidden behind it so that both stay readable.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md section 5.3 (R1 rows, evidence template and thresholds 15 and 40 percent) and server/review/rules-core.ts, rules.ts and test-support.ts.

In server/review/rules-core.ts add rule R1 for every text layer and the layer with role 'product': at each sample frame where the text layer's opacity is >= 0.3 and the product is visible, coverage = deps.maskCoverage (used only when it is provided AND meta.director.layers[productLayerId].maskAssetId exists; the region is the intersection mapped into normalised mask coordinates through the product box) else intersection area of the two boxes divided by the text box area. When the text layer's drawIndex is GREATER than the product's (text in front): kind 'text-over-product', fails when coverage > 0.15. When it is LOWER (behind): kind 'text-occluded', fails when coverage > 0.40.

Report one Finding per (rule, layer, kind) at the sample with the highest coverage (ties to the earliest), with samplesFailing (scene-relative seconds = frame/30, rounded), metrics { coverage, limit }, severity 'error', id `R1:<layerId>:<kind>` and evidence like "text 's1:caption' covers 50.6% of its area with the product at 0.50 s (text 190,800 → 1730,867; product 570,238 → 1350,886)" with coordinates rounded to integers.
If there is no product layer add a skipped note { rule:'R1', sceneId, reason:'no product layer' }. Extend server/review/rules.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: Caption at y 800 (buildReviewComp caption.y 800) yields exactly one R1 finding of kind 'text-over-product' with metrics.coverage within 0.005 of 0.506 and samplesFailing [0.5,1.5,2.5,3.5]; evidence contains '50.6%'
Caption y 867 yields no R1 finding (coverage 0.140); caption y 864 yields a finding with coverage within 0.003 of 0.163

Headline behind the product ('Slow mornings, slow coffee' size 96, y 500, behind true) yields kind 'text-occluded' with coverage within 0.01 of 0.568; the 43-character headline 'Slow mornings, slow coffee, slow everything' behind the product yields no R1 finding

With product null the result has no R1 finding and skipped contains { rule:'R1', sceneId:'s1', reason:'no product layer' }

userStories.title: Rule R3: contrast against the plate
userStories.description: As a viewer, I want text that is readable against what is behind it so that captions never wash out.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md section 5.3 (R3 maths, region mapping, skips, verified numbers), server/review/contrast.ts and server/review/pixels.ts.

In server/review/rules-core.ts add rule R3 for every text layer at each sample frame where the opacity is >= 0.3: find the bg layer (role 'bg') and its LayerBox; if the bg is an image, map the text box into NORMALISED plate coordinates through the bg box (u = (x - box.left)/(box.right - box.left), clamped to 0..1; skip the sample on an empty intersection) and call deps.plateLuminance; if the bg is a shape with a static hex fill use that colour's luminance; text colour = style.fill (hex string, or the 'default' of a themed object, or the first keyframe value). ratio = ratioFromLuminance. Fail when ratio < 4.5.

One Finding per layer at the worst (lowest-ratio) sample: kind 'low-contrast', metrics { ratio, plateLuminance, required: 4.5 }, evidence like "contrast 1.25:1 (text #ffffff on plate luminance 0.79; need 4.5:1) at 0.50 s".

Add skipped notes with reasons: 'plate pixel sampler not provided' (image bg and no deps.plateLuminance), 'text has a stroke' (style.stroke with width >= 2), 'bg layer is rotated or not an image or flat shape'. userStories.title: Rule R5: timing and scene layout
userStories.description: As a viewer, I want scene lengths that match the plan so that the film is as long as promised.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md section 5.3 (R5 rows), docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 3 (Storyboard: durationSec of the film at most 30) and server/review/geometry.ts (listScenes).

In server/review/rules-core.ts add rule R5 evaluated once per film and per scene: 'scene-duration' when the scene's frames differ from round(storyboard scene durationSec * 30) by MORE than 1 frame (evidence "scene s1 lasts 150 frames but the storyboard says 4.0 s (120 frames)"; only when a storyboard is given); 'scene-gap' or 'scene-overlap' when the root precomp layer of scene i does not start at the sum of the previous scenes' frames (evidence "scene s2 starts at frame 125, expected 120 (gap of 5 frames)"); 'total-duration' when the root durationInFrames differs from the sum of scene frames or the storyboard total exceeds 30 s; 'layer-outlasts-scene' (severity 'warn') for an inner layer whose outPoint exceeds the scene's frames.

Findings carry sceneId (the film-level 'total-duration' uses the last scene id), metrics with the frame counts, and id `R5:<sceneId>:<kind>`. Extend server/review/rules.test.ts using buildReviewComp scenes and sceneFrames.
acceptanceCriteria: sceneFrames 150 with a storyboard of 4.0 s yields one 'scene-duration' finding whose evidence is exactly "scene s1 lasts 150 frames but the storyboard says 4.0 s (120 frames)"; sceneFrames 121 yields none and 122 yields one
Two scenes where the second root precomp layer starts at frame 125 instead of 120 yield 'scene-gap' with 5 frames; starting at 115 yields 'scene-overlap'
A root durationInFrames of 241 for two 120-frame scenes yields 'total-duration'; a storyboard whose scene durations sum to 31 s yields 'total-duration' mentioning 30 s
An inner layer with outPoint 130 in a 120-frame scene yields 'layer-outlasts-scene' with severity 'warn'
Without a storyboard no 'scene-duration' finding is produced but gap and overlap are still evaluated
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Computed, self-verified suggested fixes
userStories.description: As a loop author, I want numerically justified fix suggestions so that deterministic problems are fixed without asking the model.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md section 5.5 (all four fix recipes and worked numbers), docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 4a (setTransform, setText, setSceneDuration signatures) and server/review/rules-core.ts.

Create server/review/fixes.ts exporting suggestFix(finding, ctx: { comp, sceneId, boxes..., storyboard? }): { tool: string; args: Record<string, unknown> } | undefined and applyFixInMemory(comp, fix): AepCompositionJson (maps 'setTransform' -> setTransform(comp, layerId, patch), 'setText' -> setText(comp, layerId, text, style), 'setSceneDuration' -> setSceneDuration(comp, sceneId, sec) from server/authoring/api.ts).

Rules: only for a layer whose position is static and rotation is 0. R1 text-over-product: candidate bands above and below the product box with a margin of 2 percent of the scene height, inside the safe area and tall enough; choose the smaller |dy|; fix { tool:'setTransform', args:{ layerId, y: position.y + dy } }. R2: vertical overflow -> shift y into the inset; horizontal overflow on a centred anchor (anchorFrac.x between 0.4 and 0.6) -> { tool:'setTransform', args:{ layerId, scale: floor(100 * 0.98 * safeWidth / textWidth) / 100 } }; other horizontal cases -> none. R3: { tool:'setText', args:{ layerId, text: <current source>, style:{ color } } } with bestFlatTextColor only when reaches is true, else none and append ' no flat colour reaches 4.5:1; add a scrim' to the finding evidence. R5 scene-duration: { tool:'setSceneDuration', args:{ sceneId, sec: storyboard seconds } }.

In runRulesCore attach suggestedFix to each finding, but DROP a suggestion unless re-running the same rule on applyFixInMemory(comp, fix) no longer reports that finding. Extend server/review/rules.test.ts and add server/review/fixes.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: Caption at y 800 yields suggestedFix { tool:'setTransform', args:{ layerId:'s1:caption', y } } with y within 0.05 of 907.2; applying it clears the R1 finding
The 43-character size-96 centred headline yields suggestedFix setTransform with scale 0.74 and the patched composition has no R2 finding

White caption on grey-230 yields suggestedFix setText with style.color '#111111' and the patched composition has no R3 finding; on a grey-120 plate there is NO suggestedFix and the evidence contains 'scrim'
A caption with animatedY true (position keyframes) gets no suggestedFix for R1; an R4 finding never has one
A scene-duration finding (150 frames vs 4.0 s) yields { tool:'setSceneDuration', args:{ sceneId:'s1', sec:4 } } and applying it clears the finding
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Calibration fixtures and calibrate script
userStories.description: As an owner, I want a six-case calibration with a confusion table so that I can see the rules classify seeded faults exactly.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md section 5.4 (the six cases and expected findings) and server/review/test-support.ts.

Create scripts/calibrate/s05a.ts exporting async runCalibration(): Promise<Array<{ name: string; expected: string[]; actual: string[]; pass: boolean }>> and a main that prints a table and writes fixtures/s05a/calibration.md (columns: case, expected, actual, PASS/FAIL, one line summary). Cases built with buildReviewComp: clean (default), caption-over-cup (caption.y 800), low-contrast (plate grey 230), overflow (headline 'Slow mornings, slow coffee, slow everything' size 96, centred at x 960, y 100), product-late-exit (product.outFrame 60), duration-drift (sceneFrames 150 with the 4.0 s storyboard). Actual = sorted list of finding ids from runRules(comp, makeAssetReader(assets), { storyboard }).
Write each case's composition to fixtures/s05a/<case>.comp.json and its expected finding ids to fixtures/s05a/<case>.expected.json (committed, generated by the script).
Create scripts/calibrate/s05a.test.ts that runs runCalibration() and compares the written markdown with toMatchFileSnapshot('../../fixtures/s05a/calibration.md').
acceptanceCriteria: runCalibration() returns 6 entries and every entry has pass true (6/6)

clean yields actual [] ; caption-over-cup yields ['R1:s1:caption:text-over-product']; low-contrast yields ['R3:s1:caption:low-contrast']; product-late-exit yields ['R4:s1:product:product-hidden']; duration-drift yields ['R5:s1:scene-duration']; overflow yields ['R2:s1:headline:outside-safe-area']

For every case fixtures/s05a/<case>.expected.json lists exactly the finding ids runRules produces (the test fails when the lists differ in either direction); finding ids follow `<rule>:<layerId or sceneId>:<kind>`
fixtures/s05a/calibration.md exists with a table of 6 rows all marked PASS, and the script has no network or clock dependence (running it twice gives identical files)
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Determinism, purity and contract entry point
userStories.description: As a loop and chat-tool author, I want a stable public API and proof that the rules are deterministic and isomorphic so that they can run on the server and in the browser.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md section 4.1 (determinism statement) and server/review/rules-core.ts and rules.ts.

In server/review/rules.ts re-export layerBoxAt, listScenes, sampleSceneFrames, estimateTextSize, makeSharpPixelDeps, suggestFix, applyFixInMemory, runRulesCore and the types Box, Finding, RuleDeps, SkipNote, GeometryError from their modules, and write a header comment explaining how S5b and S6 call runRules(comp, assets, opts) (inputs, outputs, skipped).

Create server/review/determinism.test.ts: run runRules twice on every calibration composition and compare JSON.stringify output; assert every number in every finding's metrics has at most 2 decimals and that findings are sorted by scene order, rule, layerId; read the source text of types.ts, sample.ts, geometry.ts, text-box.ts, contrast.ts and rules-core.ts and assert none contains "from 'node:", "from 'sharp'" or a non-type import of 'reacthub-pixitweenjs'.
Verify the contract name: import { runRules } from './rules' type-checks with the signature (comp, assets, opts?).
acceptanceCriteria: Two runRules(comp, reader, { storyboard }) calls on each of the six calibration compositions produce byte-identical JSON
No finding metric has more than 2 decimal places and no finding contains NaN or Infinity
The purity test passes: the six isomorphic modules (types, sample, geometry, text-box, contrast, rules-core) contain no node: or sharp import and no runtime engine import
server/review/rules.ts exports every name listed in the steps (a test imports each and checks typeof) and runRules accepts (comp, assets, opts?)
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

readFirst: docs/engine/README.md (engine behaviour: composition JSON, Player slot props, layer kinds, effects, validation; read before writing code that touches the engine)
docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md (sections 3, 3a, 4a, 4b and section 6: decision D-10 fixes the entry point runRules(comp, assets) in server/review/rules.ts)
docs/hackathon/steps/step-05-self-review-loop/design.md (sections 4.1, 5.1-5.5 hold every formula, threshold and worked number)
metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.
For engine behaviour (composition JSON, Player, timeline, layer kinds) read docs/engine/README.md before writing code; never edit or copy engine source.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.

server/review/types.ts, sample.ts, geometry.ts, text-box.ts, contrast.ts and rules-core.ts must stay isomorphic: no 'node:' imports, no 'sharp', no runtime import of 'reacthub-pixitweenjs' (type-only imports are fine). Only pixels.ts may use sharp.
Do not use the clock or randomness anywhere in the rules; round every reported number to 2 decimals.

ui: Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

manualGates: MG-1: owner runs `npx tsx scripts/calibrate/s05a.ts` after merge and checks fixtures/s05a/calibration.md shows 6/6 (offline, free).
MG-2: if the engine-parity tests were skipped because the package root cannot be imported under Vitest, decide whether to add the ENGINE-NEEDS.md row (a pure-subpath export of the keyframe sampler).
